solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A very old sect trilled diapasons

definitions.note: defines OCTAVES, the anagram of the entry, as the preamble asks of across clues

indicators.note: a trill shakes a note back and forth, so the word it follows is shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the usual abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written, before it is shaken up

explanation.surface: An ancient religious group singing their harmonies with vibrato.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle every clue yields two words, one an anagram of the other. Across, the wordplay builds the grid entry AVOCETS (wading birds) and the definition gives its anagram OCTAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Diapason is an old musical term for the octave, the interval spanning eight notes of the scale.

clue.text: Sex aid? A person who's worn out has six!

indicators.note: has means holds as well, so the number comes straight after the worn-out person

blocks.note: taken as written
a rag can be a person as worn out and shabby as an old cloth
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cheeky joke: the exhausted man has managed six times, thanks to a little blue pill.
explanation.walkthrough: Down clues work the other way round from across: the definition gives the grid entry VIAGRA and the wordplay builds its anagram ARAGVI, a river in Georgia and one of the puzzle's two proper names.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is the brand name of a drug for erectile dysfunction, hence a sexual aid; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Worthless Scotch run out? Letter from head of restaurant follows

indicators.note: follows says the second piece comes after the first

blocks.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
the head of restaurant is the letter R, and the spelt-out name of that letter is ar

explanation.surface: A complaint that the restaurant has run out of decent whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry ORRA; the wordplay builds its anagram ROAR. Scotch here means Scottish, not whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is a Scots word meaning odd or occasional, and hence of little value or good for nothing.

clue.text: St Peter hopes a church will accommodate this

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house a guest, so the words that follow hold the letters within them

blocks.note: the letters run from inside hopes, through a, into church

explanation.surface: A wish that the church will find room for the saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry CEPHAS; the hidden word is its anagram PESACH, the Hebrew name for Passover and the puzzle's biblical proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cephas is the Aramaic name, meaning rock, that Jesus gave to the apostle Simon, better known as Peter.

clue.text: Present time short – little support around

indicators.note: around means the support is placed on either side of the shortened time

blocks.note: a tee is the small peg that supports a golf ball
HR is the short form of hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: The present moment is brief, with only a little help to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry THERE; the wordplay builds its anagram THREE. 'Present' looks like a noun for now, but it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is present is there, in attendance at the place in question.

clue.text: Piano introducing timely computer supremo, one treading the boards

indicators.note: introducing means coming first, so the piano letter leads the rest

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
early means in good time
Bill Gates, the founder of Microsoft

explanation.surface: A pianist presenting a punctual tech billionaire, who turns out to be an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry STAGE-PLAYER; the wordplay builds its two-word anagram PEARLY GATES, the gates of heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is to act in the theatre, so one doing so is a stage actor.

clue.text: Essential for process to manufacture tiny things

definitions.note: defines ATOMS, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: what is essential lies at the very core, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of process, all of to, and the start of manufacture

explanation.surface: A claim about what any manufacturing process making minute objects requires.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden word STOMA (a pore in a leaf, or a surgical opening) goes in the grid; the definition gives its anagram ATOMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms are the minute particles of matter, a byword for anything extremely small.

clue.text: What's modern, in tin? Masses and masses

indicators.note: in places the word for modern inside the symbol for tin

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
the latter is the more recent of two

explanation.surface: Asking what counts as modern in canned goods, which come in vast quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry TRENTALS; the wordplay builds its anagram SLATTERN. 'Masses and masses' sounds like a huge amount, but the masses are church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A trental is a set of thirty requiem Masses said for the dead, so trentals are many Masses indeed.

clue.text: Declaim love in class

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the word for class

blocks.note: a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A teacher telling pupils to recite love poetry in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry ORATE; the wordplay builds its anagram ROATE, an old spelling of rote.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech in a grand, rhetorical manner.

clue.text: God of old: meditation takes in pelt

indicators.note: takes in means holds within, so the pelt goes inside the meditation

blocks.note: TM is short for Transcendental Meditation
an animal's pelt is its hairy coat

explanation.surface: An ancient deity whose devotees meditate wearing animal skins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry MITHRA; the wordplay builds its anagram THAIRM, a Scots word for gut or catgut.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithra, or Mithras, was the ancient Persian deity of light whose cult spread through the Roman army.

clue.text: Advance payment, part of fine (a third)

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of fine, through a, into third

explanation.surface: A deposit paid upfront, being a third of the penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry ANTE; the hidden word is its anagram NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put up before the cards are dealt, and by extension any sum paid beforehand.

clue.text: Mischievous little one aboard ship on course, dreadnought style?

indicators.note: aboard means on a vessel, so the little one sits inside the ship letters
on means placed next to, so the course follows

blocks.note: SS stands for steamship
an elf is a small, mischievous sprite
a course is a layer of bricks or stone

explanation.surface: An imp stowed away on a battleship, sailing the way a dreadnought would.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry FEARLESSLY; the wordplay builds its anagram SELF-SLAYER. Dreadnought looks like a warship, but read as dread-nought it means fearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreadnought is literally one who fears nothing, so acting in that style means acting without any fear.

clue.text: Cleanse father's name

definitions.note: defines RINSE, the anagram of the entry

blocks.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal; the 's reads as has
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An instruction to purify the reputation of one's father.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds SIREN for the grid; the definition gives its anagram RINSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash something clean with water, a simple synonym for cleanse.

clue.text: Very upsetting, gun wings a girth badly

indicators.note: wings are the two sides, so the gun's letters flank what follows
badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out of order

blocks.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
taken as written, before it is jumbled

explanation.surface: Distress at a gun mounted on a horse whose girth strap has been fastened wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry SHATTERING; the wordplay builds its anagram STRAIGHTEN. A girth is the strap fastening a saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering news is devastating, so upsetting that it seems to break one into pieces.

clue.text: Landlord maybe shut local – slip inside

definitions.note: defines RENTIER, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: inside places the slip within the word for shut

blocks.note: tine is a dialect word meaning to shut or enclose; local marks it as regional
to err is to make a slip

explanation.surface: A pub landlord shutting up his local because of some misstep.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds TERRINE (an earthenware dish or the pâté cooked in it) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram RENTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rentier lives on income from rents or investments, and a landlord collecting rent is one example.

clue.text: Cure includes ground spar, partly purified compound (8, two words)

definitions.note: defines PEARL ASH, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: includes means the word for cure holds the other letters within it
ground up, as in a mill, so the word spar is crushed and rearranged

blocks.note: to heal is to cure
taken as written, before it is ground

explanation.surface: A mineral remedy made by grinding spar into a refined chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds HARP SEAL for the grid; the definition gives its two-word anagram PEARL ASH. Spar, a crystalline mineral, makes the surface sound like chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl ash is potassium carbonate obtained by partly refining potash, so it is a semi-purified chemical substance.

clue.text: Regarding representatives, one behind the clock imbibes liquor

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the liquor goes inside

blocks.note: a means one
behind the clock means after the expected time
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A delegate who arrives late and has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry AGENTIAL; the wordplay builds its anagram ALGINATE, a salt of alginic acid from seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agential is the adjective from agent, describing what pertains to an agent who acts on behalf of another.

clue.text: Palm, wherein big cat conceals its head

definitions.note: defines THENAR, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: hiding its head means the first letter of the big cat is not shown

blocks.note: a panther is a big cat, a leopard

explanation.surface: A big cat hiding among palm trees, only its head out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds ANTHER (the pollen-bearing part of a stamen) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram THENAR. 'Palm' wants to be a tree, but it is the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thenar is the anatomical name for the palm of the hand, or the fleshy mound at the base of the thumb.

clue.text: Spat, look, returning? Get agitated about that

definitions.note: defines GAITER, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for look is read from right to left
agitated means stirred up, so the letters of get are jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the earlier piece

blocks.note: taken as written, before it is agitated
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone told off for a spat and a look, warned not to get worked up over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds TRIAGE for the grid; the definition gives its anagram GAITER. 'Spat' wants to be a quarrel, but it is the ankle covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a short gaiter covering the instep and ankle, worn over a shoe.

clue.text: Log, see, returning one of several plant communities

definitions.note: defines ALTERNE, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for see is read backwards

blocks.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
la is an old exclamation meaning look! or see!

explanation.surface: Instructions to record an observation on returning from a botanical survey.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds ENTERAL (relating to the intestine) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram ALTERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alterne is an ecology term for one of two or more distinct vegetation types that adjoin and alternate with each other.

clue.text: Egg on salt, French style? One supplies condiment

definitions.note: defines SALTER, the anagram of the entry

blocks.note: tar, in Shakespeare's sense, is to urge or incite
sel is the French word for salt

explanation.surface: A recipe query: egg sprinkled with salt the French way, and who provides the seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds TARSEL (a male hawk, also spelt tercel) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram SALTER. 'Egg' wants to be food; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A salter is a person who makes or deals in salt, the commonest seasoning.

clue.text: Partly cut off, dry before soak

indicators.note: before places the dry word ahead of the soak word

blocks.note: sec describes dry wine
to ret is to soak flax or hemp to loosen the fibres

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions: trim part away, dry it, then leave it to soak.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry RESECT; the wordplay builds its anagram SECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: To resect is the surgical term for removing part of an organ or bone, so it is to excise a portion.

clue.text: Mum's captivated by narrative of canal opening

definitions.note: defines MEATAL, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: someone captivated by something is held by it, so the narrative holds the mother

blocks.note: a tale is a narrative
ma is mum; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A mother enthralled by the story of a canal's grand opening day.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds TAMALE (a Mexican dish of dough steamed in a husk) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram MEATAL. 'Canal opening' sounds like a ceremony on a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatal is the adjective from meatus, the anatomical name for a passage or its opening in the body.

clue.text: Cigar, short length, exceedingly round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for exceedingly wraps the short length

blocks.note: amain is an old word meaning exceedingly or with full force
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A description of a stubby cigar, very round in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry MANILA; the wordplay builds its anagram ALMAIN, an old German dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manila is a cheroot made in the Philippines, named after its capital city.

clue.text: Segmented pipe stuck into thorny tree

indicators.note: stuck into means pushed inside, so the pipe goes within the tree

blocks.note: the bel, or bael, is a thorny Indian fruit tree
an oat is a shepherd's pipe made from an oat straw

explanation.surface: A divided pipe jammed into a prickly tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry LOBATE; the wordplay builds its anagram BOATEL, a waterside hotel for boat owners.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobate means having lobes, as a leaf divided into rounded sections does.

clue.text: Gutsy bird tucked into ale, tiddly

definitions.note: defines ENTERAL, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: tucked into places the bird inside the other letters
tiddly means slightly drunk, so the word ale staggers into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before it is made tiddly
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A brave bird getting stuck into the beer and ending up tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds ETERNAL for the grid; the definition gives its anagram ENTERAL. 'Gutsy' wants to mean brave, but it means relating to the guts.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral means relating to the intestine, so it is gutsy in the most literal sense.

clue.text: A court case ends early – rope called for

indicators.note: ending early means stopping short, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
a trial is a case heard in court

explanation.surface: A trial is cut short and the hangman's rope is demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry RIATA; the wordplay builds its anagram ATRIA, chambers of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a lariat, the rope used by cowboys for lassoing cattle.

clue.text: Hymns ancient god in Greek island

definitions.note: defines CAROLS, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: in places the god within the name of the island

blocks.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: Songs of praise to an old deity sung on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds CLAROS (an ancient Ionian site of an oracle of Apollo, one of the puzzle's two proper names) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram CAROLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Carols are joyful songs of praise, especially Christmas songs, so they are a kind of hymn.

clue.text: Poet's cadaver beginning to crumble, very much on the outside

indicators.note: beginning to keeps only the opening letter of the next word
on the outside means the word for very much goes round the chosen letter

blocks.note: sore is an old adverb meaning greatly, as in sore afraid
its first letter

explanation.surface: A poet's corpse starting to fall apart, badly on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry CORSE; the wordplay builds its anagram SCORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corse is an archaic, poetic form of corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Nun relaxes around middle of confiteor

definitions.note: defines SISTER, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letter of the following word
around means the word for relaxes encloses the chosen letter

blocks.note: to rest is to relax
the fifth of its nine letters

explanation.surface: A nun unwinding partway through the Confiteor prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds RESITS for the grid; the definition gives its anagram SISTER. The Confiteor is the Latin prayer of confession said at Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is addressed as Sister, the title for a woman in a religious order.

clue.text: US rankers putting on eastern judo kit

definitions.note: defines GIES, not the grid entry, which breaks the down-clue rule

indicators.note: putting on clothes means wearing them around you, so the soldiers enclose the letter

blocks.note: GIs are American enlisted soldiers
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: American soldiers wearing Japanese martial-arts outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue breaks the down rule: both definition and wordplay give GIES, the anagram, while the grid entry EGIS (a variant of aegis, protection) goes undefined.
explanation.definitionFit: A gi is the loose jacket and trousers worn for judo and karate, and gies is its plural.

clue.text: Cheese centre in Ilchester coated with nuts

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
coated with means covered on all sides, so the nuts word wraps round the letter

blocks.note: nuts means crazy
the fifth of its nine letters

explanation.surface: A cheese ball from Ilchester rolled in chopped nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the grid entry EDAM; the wordplay builds its anagram MEAD. Ilchester is a Somerset village that gives its name to a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese sold in balls with a red wax rind.

clue.text: Lampoonery: after orgy I misled backward boy

definitions.note: defines GOLIARDY, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: letters that are misled have gone astray, so they come out in a new order
backward tells us to read the word for boy from right to left
after places the boy at the end, following the earlier letters

blocks.note: taken as written, before being misled
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A satirist confessing that, after a wild party, he led a slow-witted boy astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds GYROIDAL (spiral in arrangement) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram GOLIARDY. 'Backward' looks like it describes the boy as slow, but it reverses him.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliardy is the satirical Latin verse of the goliards, wandering medieval scholars who mocked the Church.

clue.text: Delicate, ingesting odds and ends causing nasty spasms

definitions.note: defines TETANIC, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: something ingesting takes another thing inside it

blocks.note: nice can mean delicate or finely judged, as in a nice distinction
tat is junk, assorted odds and ends

explanation.surface: A sensitive stomach swallowing scraps and suffering painful cramps.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds NICTATE (to wink) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram TETANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanic means relating to tetanus or tetany, conditions marked by painful involuntary muscle contractions.

clue.text: Time in drama portraying particular character?

definitions.note: defines TYPAL, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for drama

blocks.note: a play is a drama
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An actor's moment on stage in a play, portraying a specific role.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds PLATY (a small aquarium fish) for the grid; the definition gives its anagram TYPAL. 'Character' sounds like a role in the drama, but it means type.
explanation.definitionFit: Typal means representative of a type, so it portrays a distinctive kind or nature.

clue.text: Second pork pie, minimal

definitions.note: defines LEAST, the anagram of the entry

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
pork pie is rhyming slang for lie, and a tale is a lie

explanation.surface: A second pork pie, but only a very small one.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds STALE for the grid; the definition gives its anagram LEAST. Pork pie is British rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest in amount or degree, the same idea as the barest minimum.

clue.text: Chap takes turn cutting grass – far from straight course

definitions.note: defines MEANDER, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: taking a turn means turning round, so the word for chap faces the other way
cutting means slicing into, so the turned word goes inside the grass

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A man mowing the grass in a wobbly line, nowhere near straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds RENAMED for the grid; the definition gives its anagram MEANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a winding bend in a river or path, the opposite of a direct route.
